newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe drought fears may spark import feed demand.
newsitem.headline: Europe drought fears may spark import feed demand.

text.p: European meals and feeds traders will be closely watching weather reports this week as drought fears mount, possibly sparking extra demand for imported feeds, market sources said on Monday.
"For the moment it's a psychological factor but if the current situation continues then it will turn into a real market factor," said Arie van Dijk, analyst at Stigevo.

The lack of rain, combined with mild temperatures, has raised fears of drought among French farmers, pushed the government to impose partial irrigation bans in some places and boosted the price of French grain on international markets.

Van Dijk said that in the countries worst affected -- Spain, Portugal and France -- high grain prices could spark extra offtake for tapioca, corn glutenfeed and citrus pulp for inclusion in cattle and pig feed.
The Dutch market was focused on the possible impact of the swine fever epidemic, which had so far led to the destruction of around one million pigs.
Van Dijk estimated a 10 percent reduction in demand for pig feed up to the end of the year, which might dent offtake of tapioca, sunflowerseed meal and rapemeal.

The market had begun the week quietly, with traders in Rotterdam saying the slightly weaker dollar might also prompt buying, although they noted that the dollar was still very high in historical terms.

Physical traders remained uncertain over the direction of Chicago futures, which was keeping consumers wary of making large purchases. Some said, however, that high wheat futures might direct a little more interest towards imported feeds.
